items.title: Saudi coalition command replaced after Bab el-Mandeb retreat intensifies dual-chokepoint risk
items.summary: Saudi Arabia replaced its Yemen coalition commander on November 16 after government-aligned forces withdrew from near Bab el-Mandeb on November 15. Reuters reports further Houthi advances; MARAD already warns increased coastline control raises risks to shipping. Hormuz tanker attacks add a second chokepoint threat, but incremental physical oil-export losses have not been verified.

observations.label: Political and security developments, November 16
observations.value: Reuters: Saudi coalition leadership replaced; military sources describe Houthi gains along southern Yemeni coast after November 15 Bab el-Mandeb retreat

observations.label: Brent intraday snapshot, November 16 10:54 AM EST
observations.value: Approximately $93.65 per barrel, -2.29% versus prior settlement, per TankerBrief delayed quote; not a closing or settlement figure

observations.label: Hormuz security context, November 16 00:58 AM EST (05:58 UTC)
observations.value: UKMTO 207-26: tanker struck by unknown projectile outbound, engine-room fire, no reported casualties; cargo or export-volume impacts unverified

observations.label: Physical-flow status
observations.value: No independently corroborated incremental export loss or contemporary ship-transit counts attributable to November 16 coastal developments

observations.label: Next checks and invalidation
observations.value: UKMTO/MARAD incidents, Bab el-Mandeb transits, AIS caveats, insurance and freight quotes, Yanbu loadings, Brent/WTI and XLE/XOP; continued normal traffic and loadings would weaken escalation risk, while verified cargo disruptions strengthen it

items.key_finding: Saudi battlefield retreat and command change increase Red Sea shipping exposure, without proof of a fresh sustained oil-flow outage.

items.title: CG Oncology rises after Phase 3 bladder cancer efficacy data
items.summary: CG Oncology announced that PIVOT-006 met its primary endpoint, reducing bladder-cancer recurrence risk compared with surveillance following surgery. Shares rose sharply during regular trading. Durability, regulatory clearance and commercial execution remain unresolved.

observations.label: November 16, 11:31 AM ET, intraday
observations.value: CGON $82.90, +11.42% versus previous close (Nexqual); not a closing move

observations.label: Clinical catalyst
observations.value: Hazard ratio 0.32, indicating 68% lower recurrence hazard; p<0.0001, median follow-up 17 months; company reports no Grade 3+ treatment-related adverse events

observations.label: Fundamental assessment
observations.value: Potential expansion into earlier-stage bladder cancer adjuvant treatment if FDA approves

observations.label: Risks, invalidation and next indicators
observations.value: Detailed trial results December 2, durability, full safety data, FDA submission/review and competition; failed approval or weakened long-term efficacy undermines thesis

items.key_finding: A pivotal oncology readout and material intraday gain warrant close regulatory follow-up.

sources.title: CG Oncology official PIVOT-006 November 16 release

items.title: Quebecor acquisition proposal triggers TELUS repricing
items.summary: Quebecor publicly disclosed a conditional, non-binding cash-and-share proposal to acquire TELUS. TELUS confirmed an independent review and emphasized significant Canadian regulatory and financing risks. The headline premium is not a binding or guaranteed realization.

observations.label: November 16, 9:30 AM ET intraday opening print
observations.value: TU opened $9.61 versus $8.53 on November 13, approximately +12.7%; opening quote, not a closing price (StockTitan)

observations.label: Offer terms using November 13 valuation
observations.value: C$6.35 cash plus 0.1700 Quebecor Class B shares per TELUS share; company-estimated value C$19.45 per share and approximately 60% premium to prior Toronto close; stock consideration value fluctuates

observations.label: Fundamental assessment
observations.value: Potential national telecom consolidation and synergies versus material spectrum, competition, financial leverage and governance constraints

observations.label: Risks, invalidation and next indicators
observations.value: TELUS special committee, binding terms, regulatory approvals, spectrum remedies and Quebecor funding; withdrawal or prohibitive conditions could eliminate deal premium

items.key_finding: A public takeover proposal creates material price dislocation with substantial approval and execution risk.

items.title: Helus Phase 3 efficacy contrasts with sharp intraday decline
items.summary: Helus reported a statistically significant 7.6-point placebo-adjusted depression-score benefit at Week 6, sustained at Week 12. A timestamped 10:01 AM ET quote showed HELP down 19.62% intraday. Safety, financing and confirmatory-trial risks remain.

observations.label: Clinical efficacy
observations.value: Week 6 MADRS placebo-adjusted -7.6 points, p<0.0001; Week 12 -7.0 points

observations.label: Risks and next checks
observations.value: Three treatment-related serious adverse events; full safety data, financing and EMBRACE replication

items.key_finding: Positive pivotal efficacy and sharp intraday weakness warrant monitoring safety and financing.

items.title: AI-sector selling broadens in US cash trading
items.summary: US chip and cloud-infrastructure shares extended their slide in Monday cash trading. The Nasdaq fell 2.1% at 10:15 a.m. ET, with AMD, Broadcom and CoreWeave weaker. Leadership and export-policy uncertainty are weighing on valuations ahead of Nvidia earnings, but weaker underlying chip demand is not yet established.

observations.label: November 16, 10:15 a.m. ET intraday snapshot
observations.value: Nasdaq -2.1%; S&P 500 -1.3%; NVDA -1.7%; AVGO -4.7%; AMD -4.7%; CRWV -6.4%; GEV -2.8% (AP); not closing prices

observations.label: Fundamentals
observations.value: Valuation, AI spending and governance concerns; customer order or shipment contraction not independently demonstrated

observations.label: Next checks and invalidation
observations.value: Nvidia earnings and guidance, export policy, chip orders, tech breadth and data-center project backlogs; resilient demand and price stabilization would weaken the selloff thesis

items.key_finding: AI-sector weakness has carried into cash-market trading, without proof of demand destruction.
